name: PostGIS
license: GPL-2.0-or-later (bundled pieces under MIT/X, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0; links GEOS LGPL, PROJ and GDAL MIT)
free_limits: none (runs inside the existing Supabase Postgres; uses database disk and compute)
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: GPL applies only if you distribute PostGIS or a modified copy; calling it by SQL from a private web app does not place the app under GPL
verification_note: LICENSE.TXT read in postgis/postgis: 'GNU General Public License, either version 2 or (at your option) any later version'. GitHub detects GPL-2.0. Supabase docs page 'PostGIS: Geo queries' returned 200 and documents 'create extension postgis with schema "extensions"'.

name: pgRouting
license: GPL-2.0-or-later (some Boost extensions under BSL-1.0, some contributed code MIT-X)
free_limits: none; needs PostGIS enabled and a routable road network loaded into tables (not supplied)
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: GPL applies on distribution of the extension, not on a private app that queries it
verification_note: LICENSE is GPL v2 text; README 'LICENSE' section states GPL-2.0-or-later for most features. Supabase docs page 'pgrouting: Geospatial Routing' returned 200 and documents 'create extension pgrouting cascade'.

name: pgvector
free_limits: none; index memory and build time grow with row count and vector dimension
verification_note: LICENSE read: PostgreSQL Licence text (Portions Copyright PostgreSQL Global Development Group). GitHub shows NOASSERTION only because its detector does not match the text. Supabase docs page 'pgvector: Embeddings and vector similarity' returned 200; extension name to enable is 'vector'.

name: PGroonga
license: PostgreSQL (the Groonga engine it links is LGPL-2.1)
free_limits: none; Groonga indexes are larger than native GIN indexes
verification_note: COPYING and README read: 'released under PostgreSQL license'. groonga/groonga COPYING is LGPL 2.1. Supabase docs page 'PGroonga: Multilingual Full Text Search' returned 200 and documents 'create extension pgroonga with schema extensions'.

name: pg_partman
provider: pg_partman (Snowflake / formerly Crunchy Data, Keith Fiske)
free_limits: none; the parent table must already be declared partitioned, and maintenance is scheduled with pg_cron
verification_note: LICENSE.txt read: 'released under the PostgreSQL License'; copyright now lists Snowflake, Inc. (2025-2026) after Crunchy Data. Supabase docs page 'pg_partman: partition management' returned 200 and documents 'create extension if not exists pg_partman with schema partman'.

name: pgTAP
free_limits: none
verification_note: The repository has no LICENSE file; the licence is the 'Copyright and License' section of README.md, which is the PostgreSQL Licence wording ('Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software ... without fee'). Supabase docs page 'pgTAP: Unit Testing' returned 200 and documents 'create extension pgtap with schema extensions'.

name: plpgsql_check
free_limits: none
verification_note: LICENSE read: the text is the MIT licence ('Permission is hereby granted, free of charge ... to deal in the Software without restriction'), not the PostgreSQL Licence it is often assumed to carry. Supabase docs page 'plpgsql_check: PL/pgSQL Linter' returned 200 and documents 'create extension plpgsql_check'.

name: PGAudit
free_limits: none; audit rows go to the Postgres log, so volume and retention follow the project's log limits
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'This code is released under the PostgreSQL licence'. Supabase docs page 'PGAudit: Postgres Auditing' returned 200 and documents 'create extension pgaudit'.

name: index_advisor
free_limits: none; requires hypopg
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The PostgreSQL License, Copyright (c) 2023, Supabase'. README: 'Requires Postgres with hypopg installed'. Supabase docs page 'index_advisor: query optimization' returned 200 and documents 'create extension index_advisor'.

name: HypoPG
free_limits: none; hypothetical indexes live only in the session that created them
verification_note: LICENSE read: PostgreSQL Licence text. Supabase docs page 'HypoPG: Hypothetical indexes' returned 200 and documents 'create extension hypopg with schema extensions'.

name: pg_jsonschema
free_limits: none
verification_note: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0 (GitHub also detects Apache-2.0). Supabase docs page 'pg_jsonschema: JSON Schema Validation' returned 200 and documents 'create extension pg_jsonschema with schema extensions'.

name: pgmq (Supabase Queues)
provider: pgmq project (originally Tembo); Supabase Queues by Supabase
free_limits: none; needs Supabase Postgres 15.6.1.143 or later; every queue adds two tables in the pgmq schema
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The PostgreSQL License, Copyright (c) 2023, Tembo'. github.com/tembo-io/pgmq now redirects (301) to github.com/pgmq/pgmq. Supabase pages read: extensions/pgmq (200, points to Queues), guides/queues (200, 'built on the pgmq database extension') and queues/quickstart ('pgmq extension is available in Postgres version 15.6.1.143 or later').

name: pg_net (Database Webhooks)
free_limits: none; the docs mark the pg_net API as beta (function signatures may change); requests are asynchronous
verification_note: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0. Supabase pages read: extensions/pg_net (200, 'Caution: The pg_net API is in beta') and guides/database/webhooks (200, 'a convenience wrapper around triggers using the pg_net extension'). The webhooks page also warns that any role that can log in can read a secret header while the request waits in net.http_request_queue.

name: pg_cron (Supabase Cron)
provider: Citus Data (Microsoft); Supabase Cron by Supabase
free_limits: none; Supabase recommends no more than 8 jobs running concurrently and each job under 10 minutes
verification_note: LICENSE read: PostgreSQL Licence wording, Copyright (c) 2015 Citus Data (GitHub detects PostgreSQL). Supabase pages read: extensions/pg_cron (200, points to Cron) and guides/cron (200, 'uses the pg_cron Postgres database extension', '8 Jobs' and '10 minutes' guidance).

name: Supabase Vault (supabase_vault)
free_limits: none; the encryption key is per project and managed by Supabase, so secrets copied to a new project by pg_dump cannot be decrypted without moving the root key
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'Supabase Vault License' = Apache License 2.0. Supabase docs page 'Vault' (guides/database/vault) returned 200: 'a Postgres extension and accompanying Supabase UI'. There is no page under /extensions/ for it (404); the Vault guide is the documentation.

name: pg_trgm + fuzzystrmatch + unaccent
free_limits: none; trigram GIN/GiST indexes add disk and write cost
verification_note: postgresql.org licence page read: 'released under the PostgreSQL License, a liberal Open Source license, similar to the BSD or MIT licenses'. Supabase has no dedicated page for these three (each /extensions/<name> is 404), but the rendered 'Postgres Extensions Overview' full list contains cards for pg_trgm, fuzzystrmatch and unaccent, the last two linking to postgresql.org docs.

name: splinter (Supabase Postgres linter)
free_limits: none; lints that depend on API exposure default to the public schema unless pgrst.db_schemas is set
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The PostgreSQL License, Copyright (c) 2024, Supabase'. Splinter is NOT a Postgres extension: the README describes a set of SQL lint queries shipped as one file (splinter.sql), so there is nothing to enable and no /extensions/ page (404). Supabase documents the same lints as 'Advisors' (guides/database/database-advisors and /database-linter both returned 200). Project docs: supabase.github.io/splinter.

name: MapLibre GL JS
free_limits: none (self-hosted library); it draws tiles but supplies none, so a tile source is still needed
verification_note: LICENSE.txt read: three-clause BSD text ('Neither the name of MapLibre GL JS nor the names of its contributors may be used to endorse'), Copyright (c) 2023 MapLibre contributors. GitHub shows NOASSERTION only because the file carries extra notices.

name: PMTiles + Protomaps basemaps
license: BSD-3-Clause for the PMTiles reference implementations (the specification is public domain / CC0); protomaps/basemaps code BSD-3-Clause, visual design CC0; the basemap tiles are an ODbL-1.0 Produced Work from OpenStreetMap
free_limits: none (self-hosted file). Full planet is roughly 120 GB at zoom 0-15; no size is documented for an Egypt or any country extract. Each extra zoom level roughly doubles the size, and 'pmtiles extract' with --maxzoom cuts a region
commercial_use: allowed; the map must show OpenStreetMap attribution (ODbL)
hosting_required: none (library) plus one static file on object storage or a CDN that supports HTTP range requests
verification_note: PMTiles LICENSE and basemaps LICENSE.md read. Protomaps downloads page read: 'distributed as an Open Database License Produced Work (OpenStreetMap attribution required)' and 'A full planet file is roughly 120 gigabytes'. The Egypt extract size is NOT documented anywhere I opened; it has to be measured by running the extract.

name: OSRM (osrm-backend)
license: BSD-2-Clause (routing data comes from OpenStreetMap, ODbL-1.0)
free_limits: Public demo server is NOT for production: 'restricted to reasonable, non-commercial use-cases', at most 1 request per second, 'no guarantees wrt. uptime, latency, or data updates'. Self-hosting has no limit
commercial_use: allowed for the software; the public demo server is restricted to non-commercial use
hosting_required: needs its own server/container; RAM depends on the size of the map extract and is not documented per country
verification_note: LICENSE.TXT read: two-clause BSD text, Copyright (c) 2017 Project OSRM contributors (GitHub detects BSD-2-Clause). Demo-server wiki page read for the usage policy quoted in free_limits.

name: Photon geocoder
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Planet database needs about 95 GB disk and 'at least 64GB RAM are recommended'; dumps are also published for selected countries, which are far smaller
commercial_use: allowed; OpenStreetMap attribution for the data
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Java); 64 GB RAM recommended for the planet, less for a country extract (no figure documented)
verification_note: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0; README 'License' section says the same. RAM and disk figures quoted from the README.

name: Turf.js
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The MIT License (MIT), Copyright (c) 2019 Morgan Herlocker'. GitHub detects MIT.

name: h3-js
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
verification_note: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0. GitHub detects Apache-2.0.

name: Open Location Code (Plus Codes)
free_limits: none (self-hosted); encoding and decoding run offline with no API call
verification_note: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0. GitHub detects Apache-2.0; last push 2026-03-30.

name: Tesseract.js
provider: Project Naptha (naptha/tesseract.js); language data from tesseract-ocr
license: Apache-2.0 (tesseract-ocr/tessdata and tessdata_fast language data are also Apache-2.0)
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Arabic 'ara' data exists: about 1.7 MB gzipped in the default set tesseract.js downloads, 2.5 MB in tessdata, 1.4 MB in tessdata_fast, 12.6 MB in tessdata_best
hosting_required: none (library); runs in the browser or Node as WebAssembly
verification_note: LICENSE.md read: Apache License 2.0. Arabic confirmed by HTTP 200 on tesseract-ocr/tessdata ara.traineddata (2,494,806 bytes), tessdata_fast (1,432,056), tessdata_best (12,603,724) and the package's own 4.0.0_best_int/ara.traineddata.gz (1,661,906). tessdata and tessdata_fast LICENSE files are Apache 2.0. Accuracy on Arabic was not tested.

name: OCRmyPDF
free_limits: none (self-hosted); needs the Tesseract engine and the language pack for each language (Arabic pack installed separately)
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: MPL is file-level, so only changes to OCRmyPDF's own files must be shared if distributed
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Python command-line tool with Tesseract; Ghostscript is no longer strictly required, pypdfium2 is an alternative); RAM not documented
verification_note: LICENSE read: Mozilla Public License Version 2.0 (GitHub detects MPL-2.0). README: uses Tesseract for 'more than 100 languages'. docs/introduction.md: 'Ghostscript is no longer strictly required'.

name: Gotenberg
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Docker image bundling headless Chromium and LibreOffice); RAM not documented in the README
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) Julien Neuhart (GitHub detects MIT). README: 'A Docker-based API for PDF', current image tag gotenberg/gotenberg:9.

name: DocuSeal
license: AGPL-3.0 with Section 7(b) Additional Terms (the DocuSeal attribution must stay in interactive user interfaces); Pro features are a paid commercial licence
free_limits: Open Source on-premises is free: e-signature, multiple signers, own SMTP, webhooks, basic API, audit log. Paid-only Pro (USD 20 per user per month on-premises, billed USD 240 a year): company logo and white-label, user roles, automated reminders, SMS verification, conditional and formula fields, bulk send from spreadsheet, SAML SSO, embedded signing form and form builder, trusted signing certificate (open source signs with a self-signed certificate)
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: AGPL covers network use, so a modified DocuSeal offered to users over a network must publish its changes; running it unmodified as a separate service does not affect the calling app; the DocuSeal attribution cannot be removed without Pro
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Ruby on Rails app with its own database); RAM not documented in what was read
suggested_class: F3 free open source (Pro features are F5 paid)
verification_note: LICENSE read: GNU AGPL Version 3. LICENSE_ADDITIONAL_TERMS read: 'a covered work must retain the original DocuSeal attribution in interactive user interfaces'. README 'Pro Features' list and the pricing page read for the paid-only list and price.

name: @signpdf/signpdf (node-signpdf)
free_limits: none (self-hosted); it applies a digital signature but supplies no certificate - a P12 certificate must be provided
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2019 The Authors. GitHub detects MIT; last push 2026-11-07.

name: ical-generator
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Sebastian Pekarek. GitHub detects MIT.

name: node-qrcode (qrcode)
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
verification_note: license file read: 'The MIT License (MIT), Copyright (c) 2012 Ryan Day'. Not archived, but the last push to the repository was 2024-08-23 - it is quiet, not actively developed.

name: IBANTools
free_limits: none (self-hosted); it validates the IBAN format and check digits only, it does not confirm the account exists
verification_note: The LICENSE file is the single line 'MIT OR MPL-2.0'; package.json says "license": "MIT or MPL-2.0". Choosing MIT removes any copyleft duty.

name: ClamAV
free_limits: none (self-hosted); signature updates are free
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: GPL applies if ClamAV itself is distributed or modified; calling clamd over its socket from a separate app does not
hosting_required: needs its own server/container: documented RAM is 'Minimum: 3 GiB, Preferred: 4 GiB' - about 1.2 GiB just to load signatures, doubling to about 2.4 GiB during the daily database reload; 2 GB 'may be insufficient'
verification_note: COPYING.txt read: GNU GPL Version 2; README: 'licensed ... under the GNU General Public License, Version 2 (GPLv2)'. RAM figures quoted from the official Docker installation page. The requirement is 3-4 GiB, well above the ~1 GB often assumed.

name: file-type
free_limits: none (self-hosted); detects type from the file's leading bytes, it is not a virus scan
verification_note: license file read: MIT License, Copyright (c) Sindre Sorhus. GitHub detects MIT.

name: ZXing-JS (@zxing/library) + barcode-detector polyfill
license: Apache-2.0 (zxing-js/library); MIT (Sec-ant/barcode-detector, which runs ZXing-C++ as WebAssembly)
free_limits: none (self-hosted); zxing-js/library states it is 'in Maintenance Mode Only' - changes come only from contributed patches
verification_note: zxing-js/library LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0; package.json "license": "Apache-2.0"; README: 'Project in Maintenance Mode Only'. Sec-ant/barcode-detector LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023 Ze-Zheng Wu (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sec-ant/barcode-detector/HEAD/LICENSE); README: a Barcode Detection API polyfill that uses ZXing-C++ WebAssembly and registers only when the browser has no native BarcodeDetector.

name: Paperless-ngx
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: GPL-3.0 applies if it is distributed or modified and distributed; it is a separate standalone application, so running it beside a private app carries no duty for that app
hosting_required: needs its own server/container plus a Redis-compatible broker (Redis or Valkey) and a database; the setup guide says it runs on a Raspberry Pi with tuning; no RAM figure is documented there
verification_note: LICENSE read: GNU GPL Version 3 (GitHub detects GPL-3.0). docs.paperless-ngx.com returned 403 to the fetch, so the same setup guide was read from docs/setup.md in the repository.

name: libphonenumber-js
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
verification_note: LICENSE read: '(The MIT License) Copyright (c) 2016 @catamphetamine'. GitHub detects MIT; last push 2026-11-10.

name: Metabase (Open Source edition)
license: AGPL-3.0 for everything outside the top-level 'enterprise' directory; Metabase Commercial License for the 'enterprise' directory and the metabase-enterprise binaries
free_limits: Open Source is free with unlimited users. Paid-only: Starter USD 100 a month (2FA, support); Pro USD 575 a month plus USD 12 per user after 10 (row and column level permissions, SSO, IP allowlists, caching controls, usage analytics and auditing, white-label, multi-tenant interactive embedding); Enterprise from USD 20,000 a year. Free embeds carry a 'Powered by Metabase' badge
commercial_use: allowed with copyleft obligations: internal use of the unmodified AGPL edition is fine; modifying it and serving it over a network requires publishing the changes; embedding it inside another app without the badge needs a commercial licence
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Java) plus a production application database such as Postgres - the bundled H2 file is not for production; RAM not documented on the page read
suggested_class: F3 free open source (Pro and Enterprise features are F5 paid)
verification_note: LICENSE.txt read (AGPL outside 'enterprise', Metabase Commercial License inside; hub.docker.com/metabase/metabase is the AGPL binary). LICENSE-AGPL.txt read: GNU AGPL Version 3. metabase.com/license and /pricing read for the paid features and prices. Row-level permissions are NOT in the free edition.

name: DuckDB-Wasm
free_limits: none (self-hosted); runs in the user's browser tab, so data size is bounded by browser WebAssembly memory
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT wording, Copyright 2018-2025 Stichting DuckDB Foundation. GitHub detects MIT. The exact browser memory ceiling was not read from the docs.

name: Soda Core
license: Elastic-2.0 on the current main branch (Soda Core v4) - source-available, NOT an OSI open-source licence; the older v3 branch is Apache-2.0
free_limits: none for self-hosted internal use; Python 3.9-3.12
commercial_use: restricted: the Elastic License 2.0 allows internal use but forbids offering the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service and forbids circumventing licence-key functionality; unrestricted only on the Apache-2.0 v3 line
hosting_required: none (library); a Python command-line tool run from CI or a scheduled job
suggested_class: F3 free open source only for the Apache-2.0 v3 line; v4 is source-available (Elastic-2.0), free for internal use
verification_note: LICENSE on the default branch (main) read: 'Elastic License 2.0'. LICENSE on branch 'v3' read: Apache License 2.0. README describes main as 'Soda Core v4 open source packages'. This differs from the common belief that Soda Core is Apache-2.0.

name: tbls
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
hosting_required: none (library); a single command-line binary run from CI or a laptop against the database
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The MIT License (MIT), Copyright 2018 Ken'ichiro Oyama'. GitHub detects MIT.

name: Squawk
free_limits: none (self-hosted)
hosting_required: none (library); a command-line linter for migration files, run in CI
verification_note: There is no single LICENSE file; LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT both exist, Cargo.toml says license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT" and package.json says "(Apache-2.0 OR MIT)". GitHub detects Apache-2.0. It is not GPL-3.0, as older references state.

name: Transformers.js + intfloat/multilingual-e5-small
provider: Hugging Face (transformers.js); intfloat / Microsoft authors (the e5 model)
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Model: 12 layers, embedding size 384, input truncated at 512 tokens, 100 languages with Arabic ('ar') listed. Weights are about 470 MB full precision and about 118 MB as the quantized ONNX file used by transformers.js. Inputs need a 'query: ' or 'passage: ' prefix
hosting_required: none (library); runs in Node or the browser, holding the 118-470 MB model in memory
verification_note: transformers.js LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0. Model card README read from huggingface.co/intfloat/multilingual-e5-small/raw/main/README.md: 'license: mit', language list includes '- ar', 'This model has 12 layers and the embedding size is 384', 'Long texts will be truncated to at most 512 tokens'; config.json hidden_size 384. File sizes from the Hugging Face file listing: model.safetensors 470,641,600 bytes; Xenova/multilingual-e5-small onnx/model_quantized.onnx 118,308,185 bytes.

name: Ollama
license: MIT for the Ollama software; each model pulled through it carries its own licence
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Documented guidance: 'at least 8 GB of RAM available to run the 7B models, 16 GB to run the 13B models, and 32 GB to run the 33B models'
commercial_use: allowed for Ollama itself; check the licence of each model separately
hosting_required: needs its own server/container with at least 8 GB RAM free for a 7B model (16 GB for 13B); a GPU is optional but CPU-only replies are slow
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) Ollama. The RAM sentence is in the repository README at tags v0.5.0, v0.9.0 and v0.12.0 but has been removed from the current README; the current quickstart instead says of its example model 'about 7.2 GB ... We recommend 8 GB of available VRAM'. Required RAM also scales with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL and context length (docs/faq.mdx).

name: whisper.cpp
provider: ggml-org (Georgi Gerganov and the ggml authors); models by OpenAI
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Documented size and memory: small 466 MiB disk / about 852 MB RAM; medium 1.5 GiB / about 2.1 GB; large 2.9 GiB / about 3.9 GB (large-v3 is 2.9 GiB on disk; quantized large-v3-q5_0 is 1.1 GiB, large-v3-turbo 1.5 GiB). Arabic is a supported language
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (or a native binary on a worker): about 0.9 GB RAM for small, 2.1 GB for medium, 3.9 GB for large-v3
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors. Memory table read from README.md and disk sizes from models/README.md. Arabic confirmed in the language table in src/whisper.cpp ({ "ar", { 13, "arabic" } }) and in openai/whisper tokenizer.py. Accuracy on Egyptian Arabic was not tested.

name: Presidio
provider: Presidio contributors (originally Microsoft; repository now at data-privacy-stack/presidio)
free_limits: none (self-hosted). Out of the box it detects English only: 'In its default configuration, it contains recognizers and models for English'. Arabic needs an Arabic NLP model configured (spaCy, Stanza or transformers) plus Arabic recognizers and context words written by the adopter
hosting_required: needs its own server/container (Python service with an NLP model loaded); RAM not documented on the page read
verification_note: LICENSE read: 'The MIT License (MIT), Copyright (c) Presidio Contributors'. github.com/microsoft/presidio now answers 301 to github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio - the repository has left the Microsoft organization; the raw microsoft/presidio URLs still resolve through that redirect. Languages page read from the repository docs: Arabic is not named as supported by default.

name: Langfuse (self-hosted)

free_limits: none for the MIT core when self-hosted; a licence key is needed for the enterprise add-ons (the self-hosting page marks Organization Creators, Instance Management API and UI Customization as EE)
commercial_use: allowed for the MIT core; enterprise directories need a paid licence

Langfuse's core is permissively licensed (MIT license)'. Component list read from langfuse.com/self-hosting.

name: promptfoo
free_limits: none (self-hosted); evaluations run locally, the only cost is the model calls the tests make
hosting_required: none (library); a command-line tool run locally or in CI
verification_note: LICENSE read: MIT wording, 'Copyright (c) Promptfoo 2025' (GitHub detects MIT). README: 'Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI. Promptfoo remains open source and MIT licensed.'
